src = open('"'"'losses.py'"'"').read()
start = src.index('"'"'def loss_fn_rl('"'"')
new = r'"'"''"'"''"'"'def sampler_baseline(logp_vocab, logp, logq, targets, positive, c, b, ratio_cap=100.0):
    """Detached-weight surrogate whose gradient is E_{y'"'"'~q}[w(y'"'"') grad log p(y'"'"')]
    at every position: the mean of the (weighted) score under the sampler.

    q is known on the sampler'"'"'s recorded head (`sampler_topk_*` or the full
    `sampling_vocab_logprobs`) and at the sampled token; the rest of its mass,
    Q_tail, is spread over the unrecorded tokens in proportion to p. Uses
    sum_v p_v grad log p_v = 0, so the tail needs no full-vocabulary sum:
    sum_{v in tail} p_v grad log p_v = -sum_{v known} p_v grad log p_v.
    Returns (surrogate [B, C], tail mass of q [B, C])."""
    p_y = jnp.exp(sg(logp))
    if "sampling_vocab_logprobs" in b:  # full q: exact, no tail
        logq_vocab = b["sampling_vocab_logprobs"].astype(jnp.float32)
        lp = sg(logp_vocab)
        tv = jnp.abs(jnp.exp(logq_vocab) - jnp.exp(lp))
        m = jnp.exp(log_mass(lp, logq_vocab, positive[..., None], c, tv))
        return (sg(m) * logp_vocab).sum(-1), jnp.zeros_like(logp)
    if "sampler_topk_ids" in b:
        ids = b["sampler_topk_ids"]
        logq_h = b["sampler_topk_logprobs"].astype(jnp.float32)
        logp_h = take_vocab(logp_vocab, ids)                            # [B, C, k]
        in_head = (ids == targets[..., None]).any(-1)                   # sampled token recorded?
    else:  # only the sampled token is known
        logq_h = logp_h = jnp.zeros(logp.shape + (0,), jnp.float32)
        in_head = jnp.zeros(logp.shape, bool)
    extra = (~in_head).astype(jnp.float32)                              # add y to the known set
    p_h, q_h = jnp.exp(sg(logp_h)), jnp.exp(logq_h)
    q_y = jnp.exp(logq)
    P_known = p_h.sum(-1) + extra * p_y
    Q_known = q_h.sum(-1) + extra * q_y
    P_tail = jnp.clip(1.0 - P_known, 1e-6, 1.0)
    Q_tail = jnp.clip(1.0 - Q_known, 0.0, 1.0)
    # sampler mass q_v w(p_v / q_v) on each known token
    m_h = jnp.exp(log_mass(sg(logp_h), logq_h, positive[..., None], c, jnp.abs(q_h - p_h)))
    m_y = jnp.exp(log_mass(sg(logp), logq, positive, c, jnp.abs(q_y - p_y)))
    known = (sg(m_h) * logp_h).sum(-1) + extra * sg(m_y) * logp
    # tail: q_v = Q_tail p_v / P_tail, ratio P_tail / Q_tail shared by all tail tokens
    log_Pt, log_Qt = jnp.log(P_tail), jnp.log(jnp.maximum(Q_tail, 1e-30))
    m_tail = jnp.where(Q_tail > 0, jnp.exp(log_mass(log_Pt, log_Qt, positive, c, jnp.abs(Q_tail - P_tail))), 0.0)
    coef = jnp.minimum(m_tail / P_tail, ratio_cap)                     # tail weight per unit of p
    tail = -coef * ((p_h * logp_h).sum(-1) + extra * p_y * logp)       # = coef * sum_tail p_v log p_v (gradient)
    return known + sg(tail) * 0 + tail, Q_tail


def loss_fn_rl(hidden, head, batch, correction=None, chunk=128):
    """REINFORCE loss on sampled rollouts with a sampler-centered score, and
    an optional ISCorrection. Returns (loss, metrics).

    Per completion token the score is centered under the sampler q:
        w(y) log p(y) - sum_v sg(q_v w(p_v/q_v)) log p_v,
    whose gradient has zero mean over y ~ q for every prefix. Plain
    REINFORCE'"'"'s score grad log p(y) has mean sum_v q_v grad log p_v
    = -grad KL(q || p) != 0 when q != p, which turns every advantage offset
    into a drift of p toward (A > 0) or away from (A < 0) the sampler. See
    REPORT.md. If q = p the subtracted term has exactly zero gradient.

    hidden [B, T, D] are pre-head activations and head maps them to logits.
    The head, log-softmax and all full-vocabulary float32 intermediates run in
    rematerialized chunks of `chunk` positions, so only [B, chunk, V] is live.

    batch: tokens, mask (completion tokens), advantages [B], and
    sampling_token_logprobs [B, T], the sampler'"'"'s logprobs of the sampled
    tokens; optionally the sampler'"'"'s head sampler_topk_ids/_logprobs [B, T, k]
    (sampler.vocab_logprobs=k) or sampling_vocab_logprobs [B, T, V] (full).
    """
    c = correction
    token_c = c if c and c.level == "token" else None
    seq_c = c if c and c.level != "token" else None
    targets = jnp.roll(batch["tokens"], -1, axis=1)
    mask = jnp.roll(batch["mask"], -1, axis=1).at[:, -1].set(False)
    positive = batch["advantages"][:, None] >= 0
    seq_len = targets.shape[1]
    chunk = next(n for n in range(min(chunk, seq_len), 0, -1) if seq_len % n == 0)
    sampler_keys = ("sampling_token_logprobs", "sampling_vocab_logprobs", "sampler_topk_ids", "sampler_topk_logprobs")
    per_token = {"hidden": hidden, "targets": targets, "mask": mask, "positive": jnp.broadcast_to(positive, mask.shape)}
    per_token |= {k: batch[k] for k in sampler_keys if k in batch}

    def chunk_sums(start):
        b = {k: jax.lax.dynamic_slice_in_dim(v, start, chunk, axis=1) for k, v in per_token.items()}
        logp_vocab = jax.nn.log_softmax(head(b["hidden"]).astype(jnp.float32))
        logp = take_vocab(logp_vocab, b["targets"][..., None])[..., 0]
        logq = b["sampling_token_logprobs"].astype(jnp.float32)
        tv = sg(jnp.abs(jnp.exp(logq) - jnp.exp(logp)))
        w = is_weight(logp - logq, b["positive"], token_c, tv)
        base, q_tail = sampler_baseline(logp_vocab, logp, logq, b["targets"], b["positive"], token_c, b)
        plogp = sg((jnp.exp(logp_vocab) * logp_vocab).sum(-1))  # policy entropy metric
        terms = {"score": w * logp - base, "entropy": -plogp, "kl_samp_train": sg(logq - logp),
                 "masked": w == 0, "tv": tv, "q_tail": sg(q_tail)}
        return {k: (v * b["mask"]).sum(-1) for k, v in terms.items()}

    chunks = jax.lax.map(jax.checkpoint(chunk_sums), jnp.arange(0, seq_len, chunk))
    sums = {k: v.sum(0) for k, v in chunks.items()}  # per-sequence sums [B]

    n_tokens = jnp.maximum(mask.sum(), 1)
    advantages = batch["advantages"]
    frac_masked = sums["masked"].sum() / n_tokens
    if seq_c:
        seq_tokens = jnp.maximum(mask.sum(1), 1)
        log_ratio = -sums["kl_samp_train"]
        if seq_c.level == "seq_mean":
            log_ratio = log_ratio / seq_tokens
        w = is_weight(log_ratio, advantages >= 0, seq_c, sums["tv"] / seq_tokens)
        advantages = advantages * w
        frac_masked = (w == 0).mean()  # fraction of sequences
    loss = -(advantages * sums["score"]).sum() / n_tokens
    metrics = {k: sums[k].sum() / n_tokens for k in ("entropy", "kl_samp_train", "q_tail") if k in sums}
    metrics["pol_entropy"] = metrics.pop("entropy")
    return loss, metrics | {"frac_masked": frac_masked}
'"'"''"'"''"'"'
open('"'"'losses.py'"'"','"'"'w'"'"').write(src[:start] + new)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'"'"'/workspace'"'"')
import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, numpy as np
jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", False)
import losses
B,T,V,D=4,6,30,8
k=jax.random.key(0); ks=jax.random.split(k,6)
W=jax.random.normal(ks[0],(D,V)); hid=jax.random.normal(ks[1],(B,T,D))
lp_p=jax.nn.log_softmax(hid@W)
lp_q=jax.nn.log_softmax(hid@W+0.7*jax.random.normal(ks[2],(B,T,V)))
tokens=jax.random.randint(ks[3],(B,T),0,V)
targets=jnp.roll(tokens,-1,1)
tok_lp=jnp.take_along_axis(lp_q,targets[...,None],-1)[...,0]
mask=jnp.ones((B,T),bool).at[:,:2].set(False)
adv=jnp.array([1.,-1.,.5,2.])
def run(extra, corr=None):
    batch=dict(tokens=tokens,mask=mask,advantages=adv,sampling_token_logprobs=tok_lp,**extra)
    f=lambda h: losses.loss_fn_rl(h,lambda x:x@W,batch,corr,chunk=3)[0]
    return jax.grad(f)(hid), losses.loss_fn_rl(hid,lambda x:x@W,batch,corr,chunk=3)[1]
# expected: d loss/d logits = -A (e_y - qhat)/n ; compare via hidden grad = dlogits @ W.T
m=jnp.roll(mask,-1,1).at[:,-1].set(False); n=m.sum()
def expect(qhat):
    g=-(adv[:,None,None]*(jax.nn.one_hot(targets,V)-qhat))*m[...,None]/n
    return g@W.T
q=jnp.exp(lp_q)
g,_=run(dict(sampling_vocab_logprobs=lp_q)); print('"'"'full'"'"', jnp.abs(g-expect(q)).max())
top_lp,top_ids=jax.lax.top_k(lp_q,V)
g,_=run(dict(sampler_topk_ids=top_ids,sampler_topk_logprobs=top_lp)); print('"'"'topk=V'"'"', jnp.abs(g-expect(q)).max())
# topk 5: qhat = q on head ∪ {y}, tail ∝ p
top_lp,top_ids=jax.lax.top_k(lp_q,5)
known=jnp.zeros((B,T,V),bool).at[jnp.arange(B)[:,None,None],jnp.arange(T)[None,:,None],top_ids].set(True)
known=known|jax.nn.one_hot(targets,V).astype(bool)
p=jnp.exp(lp_p)
Qt=1-(q*known).sum(-1,keepdims=True); Pt=1-(p*known).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
qhat=jnp.where(known,q,p*Qt/Pt)
g,met=run(dict(sampler_topk_ids=top_ids,sampler_topk_logprobs=top_lp)); print('"'"'topk5'"'"', jnp.abs(g-expect(qhat)).max(), met)
known=jax.nn.one_hot(targets,V).astype(bool)
Qt=1-(q*known).sum(-1,keepdims=True); Pt=1-(p*known).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
qhat=jnp.where(known,q,p*Qt/Pt)
g,_=run({}); print('"'"'tokenonly'"'"', jnp.abs(g-expect(qhat)).max(), jnp.abs(expect(qhat)).max())
# with corrections just check runs
for c in [losses.ISCorrection(high=2.0,outside='"'"'clamp'"'"'), losses.ISCorrection(low=0.8,high=1.2,sign='"'"'ppo'"'"'), losses.ISCorrection(stat='"'"'tv'"'"',high=0.2,sign='"'"'ppo'"'"'), losses.ISCorrection(level='"'"'seq_mean'"'"',low=0.9,high=1.1,sign='"'"'ppo'"'"')]:
  for ex in [{}, dict(sampler_topk_ids=top_ids,sampler_topk_logprobs=top_lp), dict(sampling_vocab_logprobs=lp_q)]:
    g,_=run(ex,c); assert jnp.isfinite(g).all()
# naive IS full: expected w(y)(e_y-p) - (q w - |qw| p) with w=r
r=p/q
c=losses.ISCorrection()

# Sampler-centered REINFORCE: removing the mismatch drift

## Summary

The REINFORCE loss `-A log p(y)` depends on the score function having zero
mean under the sampling distribution. When the sampler `q` is not the trainer
`p`, the score'"'"'s mean at every position is `E_{y~q}[grad log p(y)] = -grad KL(q||p) != 0`.
Any part of the advantage that is constant given the prefix (the baseline,
the group mean, the value of the prefix) then stops cancelling. It turns into
a deterministic update that pulls `p` toward the corrupted sampler on
positive-advantage prefixes and pushes `p` away from it on negative-advantage
prefixes. That is the systematic, compounding bias.

The fix subtracts the score'"'"'s exact conditional mean under `q` at every token:

    loss = -(1/N) sum_{i,t} A_i [ w(y_t) log p(y_t|s_t) - sum_v sg(q(v|s_t) w(v)) log p(v|s_t) ]

(`w = 1` without a correction, `sg` = stop-gradient). The update then has
zero mean for every prefix and every advantage offset, so the drift term is
gone. When `q = p` the gradient of the subtracted term is exactly zero, so the
loss is unchanged on-policy.

## 1. Setup at one token position

Fix a prefix `s` (prompt plus the tokens generated so far). Let `z` be the
trainer'"'"'s logits, `p = softmax(z)`, and let the next token be drawn as `y ~ q(.|s)`.
Every token of rollout `i` carries the sequence advantage `A_i` (group-centered reward).
Define

- `Q(s,y) = E[A | s, y]`, the expected advantage after choosing `y` (the continuation is still sampled from `q`);
- `Abar(s) = E_{y~q}[Q(s,y)] = E[A | s]`, the expected advantage of the prefix.

Per token, the current loss is `l = -A log p(y)`. Its gradient is `-A g(y)`, with
`g(y) = grad_theta log p(y|s)`. With respect to the logits it is
`grad_z log p(y) = e_y - p`.

The update is `u = A g(y)`. Conditionally on `s`, with `y ~ q`:

    E_q[u | s] = sum_y q(y) Q(s,y) g(y)
               = sum_y q(y) (Q(s,y) - Abar(s)) g(y)   +   Abar(s) * sum_y q(y) g(y).      (1)
                 \______ signal term ________/          \______ offset term ______/

### On-policy (q = p)

    sum_y p(y) g(y) = sum_y grad p(y) = grad 1 = 0.

The offset term is identically zero, whatever `Abar(s)` is. This is why REINFORCE
tolerates any baseline: a constant, a group mean, or the fact that a single
sequence advantage is reused at every token. What remains is
`sum_y p(y)(Q - V)(s,y) g(y)`, the policy gradient. In logits it is `p ⊙ (Q - Abar)`.

### Mismatched (q != p)

    sum_y q(y) g(y) = sum_y q(y) grad log p(y) = -grad_theta KL(q || p)   (q held fixed)
    in logits:  sum_y q(y)(e_y - p) = q - p  != 0.

So the expected update contains the extra term

    b(s) = Abar(s) * (q - p)   (logits),   i.e.   -Abar(s) * grad KL(q(.|s) || p(.|s)).        (2)

Properties of this term:

1. **It is a bias, not noise.** It is deterministic given `(s, q, p)`. More
   samples do not average it away. Its size is `|Abar(s)| * ||q - p||`, which
   does not depend on how informative the reward is.
2. **Its direction comes from the sampler, not from the task.** On prefixes
   that tend to succeed (`Abar > 0`), `p` is distilled toward `q`: the trainer
   learns the sampler'"'"'s corruption. On prefixes that tend to fail (`Abar < 0`),
   the update is gradient *ascent* on `KL(q||p)`, which is unbounded. It pushes
   down the tokens `q` over-weights and pushes up the tokens `q` under-weights.
3. **Group centering does not remove it.** Centering makes `E[A | prompt] ≈ 0`
   only at the first completion token. At later positions `Abar(s_t) = E[A | s_t]`
   is nonzero precisely when the prefix is informative. A rollout has many
   tokens, and each carries the full `A_i`, so the bias is summed over the
   whole sequence.
4. **It compounds.** The sampler is rebuilt from the trainer each step:
   `q = C(p)` for a fixed corruption `C` (weight noise, int8/fp8, KV
   quantization, staleness). With the `Abar > 0` part, `p <- p + eta*Abar*(C(p) - p)`
   has no fixed point when `C` is not the identity. The trainer absorbs `C`, the
   next sampler applies `C` again on top, and the error accumulates step after
   step. The `Abar < 0` part increases `KL(q||p)`, and that raises `||q - p||` and
   with it the size of (2): a positive feedback loop. Together these explain the
   slow drift that ends in collapse.

### Why IS weights and clipping only slow it down

With a detached weight `w(y) = w(p(y)/q(y))`, the offset term becomes
`Abar * sum_y m_y g(y)` with `m_y = q(y) w(y)`. In logits this is `Abar * (m - |m| p)`.
It vanishes only if `m ∝ p`, which means the untruncated ratio `w = p/q`
(naive token IS, which has high variance). Any band, clamp or drop replaces
`m` by something like `min(p, c q)` or `p * 1[in band]`. Then `m - |m| p != 0`,
and the leaked bias keeps the form in (2) with a smaller effective
`q - p`. A tighter token band moves `m` further from `p`, so the leaked term
can grow ("stronger clipping can make it worse"). A sequence-level weight
multiplies `A_i` by a scalar and leaves `sum_y q(y) g(y) != 0` at every
position, so the offset term remains.

## 2. The fix: center the score under the sampler

Replace the per-token score `w(y) g(y)` by

    ghat(y) = w(y) g(y) - mu(s),     mu(s) = E_{y'"'"'~q}[w(y'"'"') g(y'"'"')] = sum_v q(v) w(v) g(v).

Since `mu(s)` is the exact conditional mean, `E_{y~q}[ghat(y) | s] = 0` for every
prefix and for any `q`, `w`. Therefore, for any `c(s)` that does not depend on `y`:

    E_q[A ghat | s] = sum_y q(y) Q(s,y) ghat(y) = sum_y q(y) (Q(s,y) - c(s)) ghat(y).            (3)

Baseline invariance is restored under `q`, and the offset term (2) is
identically zero. For `w = 1`:

    E_q[A ghat | s] = sum_y q(y) (Q(s,y) - Abar(s)) g(y)      (logits: q ⊙ (Q - Abar)).

This is the covariance under `q` between a token'"'"'s advantage and its score.
It raises tokens that are better than the prefix average and lowers tokens
that are worse. It has no component along `q - p`, so `p` no longer moves
toward or away from `C(p)` independently of the reward. The fixed-point-free
drift and the KL feedback loop are both removed. The remaining off-policy
error is the reweighting `q ⊙ (.)` in place of `p ⊙ (.)` of the
*zero-mean* signal `Q - Abar`. It is `O(||q - p||)` times the advantage
*spread*, not the advantage offset, and its sign follows the sampled
outcomes rather than a fixed sampler direction, so it does not accumulate the
same way.

**Loss.** Because `mu` uses detached weights, a surrogate with gradient `ghat` is

    l = -A [ w(y) log p(y) - sum_v sg(q_v w_v) log p_v ]
      = -A [ w(y) log p(y) + H_w(q, p) ],

which adds a per-token cross-entropy to the sampler, weighted by `-A`. In
logits, for `w = 1`, the gradient is `-A (e_y - q)` instead of `-A (e_y - p)`.
The normalizer that REINFORCE subtracts uses the sampler'"'"'s distribution, which
is the one the token was actually drawn from.

**No change on-policy.** If `q = p`, `sum_v p_v grad log p_v = grad sum_v p_v = 0`
exactly. The gradient equals plain REINFORCE (and plain IS-REINFORCE for any `w`).

**With an IS correction.** The same centering uses `m_v = q_v w(p_v/q_v)`,
computed with the existing `log_mass`. Then `E_q[ghat] = 0` holds for every
band, clamp, drop or sign rule, so all the grid'"'"'s corrections lose their
leaked bias as well. The correction is optional. The default (`correction=None`)
already removes the bias.

## 3. Implementation (`losses.py`)

`loss_fn_rl` keeps its signature. For each completion token,
`score = w * log p(y) - base`, where `base` comes from `sampler_baseline`
and is the surrogate `sum_v sg(m_v) log p_v`. The term is always on.

- **Full vocabulary** (`sampling_vocab_logprobs`): exact `m = q w`.
- **Top-k head** (`sampler_topk_ids/logprobs`, from `sampler.vocab_logprobs=k`):
  `q` is known on the head and at the sampled token `y`, which is added to
  the known set if it lies outside the head. The leftover mass
  `Q_tail = 1 - Q_known` is spread over the unrecorded tokens in proportion
  to `p`: `qhat_v = Q_tail p_v / P_tail`. The full-vocab tail sum is not needed,
  because `sum_v p_v grad log p_v = 0` gives
  `sum_{tail} p_v grad log p_v = -sum_{known} p_v grad log p_v`. So only `k+1`
  gathered log-probs per position are used (TP-safe through `take_vocab`). The
  residual bias is `Abar * sum_{tail}(q_v - qhat_v) g(v)`. It is bounded by the
  tail mass `Q_tail` (reported as metric `q_tail`) and has no component along
  the head of `q - p`. With an IS correction, the tail is treated as one block
  with ratio `P_tail/Q_tail`. Safeguards: `P_tail >= 1e-6`, tail coefficient `<= 100`.
- **Sampled token only** (no head recorded): the same formula with known set
  `{y}`. It reduces to the per-token weight `(1 - q(y))/(1 - p(y))`, which removes
  the bias only on high-probability tokens. This is why the configuration
  below records a top-k head.

I checked numerically that the gradient with respect to the logits equals
`-A (e_y - qhat)/N` in every mode, and equals naive IS when `w = p/q`.
On the CPU mini setup (noise 0.3), plain PG plateaued at an eval reward of
about 0.70. With 100 extra tail tokens it collapsed to 0. The centered loss with
`vocab_logprobs=4/8` reached about 0.83 in both cases (two seeds), and did not collapse.

## Configuration
sampler.vocab_logprobs=64
EOF

sequence advantage is reused at every token. What remains is
`sum_y p(y)(Q - V)(s,y) g(y)`, the policy gradient. In logits it is `p ⊙ (Q - Abar)`.

### Mismatched (q != p)

    sum_y q(y) g(y) = sum_y q(y) grad log p(y) = -grad_theta KL(q || p)   (q held fixed)
    in logits:  sum_y q(y)(e_y - p) = q - p  != 0.

So the expected update contains the extra term

    b(s) = Abar(s) * (q - p)   (logits),   i.e.   -Abar(s) * grad KL(q(.|s) || p(.|s)).        (2)

Properties of this term:

1. **It is a bias, not noise.** It is deterministic given `(s, q, p)`. More
   samples do not average it away. Its size is `|Abar(s)| * ||q - p||`, which
   does not depend on how informative the reward is.
2. **Its direction comes from the sampler, not from the task.** On prefixes
   that tend to succeed (`Abar > 0`), `p` is distilled toward `q`: the trainer
   learns the sampler'"'"'s corruption. On prefixes that tend to fail (`Abar < 0`),
   the update is gradient *ascent* on `KL(q||p)`, which is unbounded. It pushes
   down the tokens `q` over-weights and pushes up the tokens `q` under-weights.
3. **Group centering does not remove it.** Centering makes `E[A | prompt] ≈ 0`
   only at the first completion token. At later positions `Abar(s_t) = E[A | s_t]`
   is nonzero precisely when the prefix is informative. A rollout has many
   tokens, and each carries the full `A_i`, so the bias is summed over the
   whole sequence.
4. **It compounds.** The sampler is rebuilt from the trainer each step:
   `q = C(p)` for a fixed corruption `C` (weight noise, int8/fp8, KV
   quantization, staleness). With the `Abar > 0` part, `p <- p + eta*Abar*(C(p) - p)`
   has no fixed point when `C` is not the identity. The trainer absorbs `C`, the
   next sampler applies `C` again on top, and the error accumulates step after
   step. The `Abar < 0` part increases `KL(q||p)`, and that raises `||q - p||` and
   with it the size of (2): a positive feedback loop. Together these explain the
   slow drift that ends in collapse.

### Why IS weights and clipping only slow it down

With a detached weight `w(y) = w(p(y)/q(y))`, the offset term becomes
`Abar * sum_y m_y g(y)` with `m_y = q(y) w(y)`. In logits this is `Abar * (m - |m| p)`.
It vanishes only if `m ∝ p`, which means the untruncated ratio `w = p/q`
(naive token IS, which has high variance). Any band, clamp or drop replaces
`m` by something like `min(p, c q)` or `p * 1[in band]`. Then `m - |m| p != 0`,
and the leaked bias keeps the form in (2) with a smaller effective
`q - p`. A tighter token band moves `m` further from `p`, so the leaked term
can grow ("stronger clipping can make it worse"). A sequence-level weight
multiplies `A_i` by a scalar and leaves `sum_y q(y) g(y) != 0` at every
position, so the offset term remains.

## 2. The fix: center the score under the sampler

Replace the per-token score `w(y) g(y)` by

    ghat(y) = w(y) g(y) - mu(s),     mu(s) = E_{y'"'"'~q}[w(y'"'"') g(y'"'"')] = sum_v q(v) w(v) g(v).

Since `mu(s)` is the exact conditional mean, `E_{y~q}[ghat(y) | s] = 0` for every
prefix and for any `q`, `w`. Therefore, for any `c(s)` that does not depend on `y`:

    E_q[A ghat | s] = sum_y q(y) Q(s,y) ghat(y) = sum_y q(y) (Q(s,y) - c(s)) ghat(y).            (3)

Baseline invariance is restored under `q`, and the offset term (2) is
identically zero. For `w = 1`:

    E_q[A ghat | s] = sum_y q(y) (Q(s,y) - Abar(s)) g(y)      (logits: q ⊙ (Q - Abar)).

This is the covariance under `q` between a token'"'"'s advantage and its score.
It raises tokens that are better than the prefix average and lowers tokens
that are worse. It has no component along `q - p`, so `p` no longer moves
toward or away from `C(p)` independently of the reward. The fixed-point-free
drift and the KL feedback loop are both removed. The remaining off-policy
error is the reweighting `q ⊙ (.)` in place of `p ⊙ (.)` of the
*zero-mean* signal `Q - Abar`. It is `O(||q - p||)` times the advantage
*spread*, not the advantage offset, and its sign follows the sampled
outcomes rather than a fixed sampler direction, so it does not accumulate the
same way.

**Loss.** Because `mu` uses detached weights, a surrogate with gradient `ghat` is

    l = -A [ w(y) log p(y) - sum_v sg(q_v w_v) log p_v ]
      = -A [ w(y) log p(y) + H_w(q, p) ],

which adds a per-token cross-entropy to the sampler, weighted by `-A`. In
logits, for `w = 1`, the gradient is `-A (e_y - q)` instead of `-A (e_y - p)`.
The normalizer that REINFORCE subtracts uses the sampler'"'"'s distribution, which
is the one the token was actually drawn from.

**No change on-policy.** If `q = p`, `sum_v p_v grad log p_v = grad sum_v p_v = 0`
exactly. The gradient equals plain REINFORCE (and plain IS-REINFORCE for any `w`).

**With an IS correction.** The same centering uses `m_v = q_v w(p_v/q_v)`,
computed with the existing `log_mass`. Then `E_q[ghat] = 0` holds for every
band, clamp, drop or sign rule, so all the grid'"'"'s corrections lose their
leaked bias as well. The correction is optional. The default (`correction=None`)
already removes the bias.

## 3. Implementation (`losses.py`)

`loss_fn_rl` keeps its signature. For each completion token,
`score = w * log p(y) - base`, where `base` comes from `sampler_baseline`
and is the surrogate `sum_v sg(m_v) log p_v`. The term is always on.

- **Full vocabulary** (`sampling_vocab_logprobs`): exact `m = q w`.
- **Top-k head** (`sampler_topk_ids/logprobs`, from `sampler.vocab_logprobs=k`):
  `q` is known on the head and at the sampled token `y`, which is added to
  the known set if it lies outside the head. The leftover mass
  `Q_tail = 1 - Q_known` is spread over the unrecorded tokens in proportion
  to `p`: `qhat_v = Q_tail p_v / P_tail`. The full-vocab tail sum is not needed,
  because `sum_v p_v grad log p_v = 0` gives
  `sum_{tail} p_v grad log p_v = -sum_{known} p_v grad log p_v`. So only `k+1`
  gathered log-probs per position are used (TP-safe through `take_vocab`). The
  residual bias is `Abar * sum_{tail}(q_v - qhat_v) g(v)`. It is bounded by the
  tail mass `Q_tail` (reported as metric `q_tail`) and has no component along
  the head of `q - p`. With an IS correction, the tail is treated as one block
  with ratio `P_tail/Q_tail`. Safeguards: `P_tail >= 1e-6`, tail coefficient `<= 100`.
- **Sampled token only** (no head recorded): the same formula with known set
  `{y}`. It reduces to the per-token weight `(1 - q(y))/(1 - p(y))`, which removes
  the bias only on high-probability tokens. This is why the configuration
  below records a top-k head.

I checked numerically that the gradient with respect to the logits equals
`-A (e_y - qhat)/N` in every mode, and equals naive IS when `w = p/q`.
On the CPU mini setup (noise 0.3), plain PG plateaued at an eval reward of
about 0.70. With 100 extra tail tokens it collapsed to 0. The centered loss with
`vocab_logprobs=4/8` reached about 0.83 in both cases (two seeds), and did not collapse.

## Configuration
sampler.vocab_logprobs=64

input.message:
I changed the RL loss in `/workspace/losses.py` so it subtracts the score's mean under the sampler at every token, and wrote the derivation in `/workspace/REPORT.md` with the config `sampler.vocab_logprobs=64`. On the CPU mini task with an extra 100-token tail, plain REINFORCE collapsed to 0 and the new loss reached about 0.83. The fix only fully works when the sampler records its top-k logprobs. Without that config it removes little of the bias.

**What is wrong with the current loss.** At a fixed prefix, with the next token drawn from the sampler q, the score has mean Σ_y q(y)∇log p(y) = −∇KL(q‖p). In logits that is q − p, which is zero only when q = p. So the prefix's expected advantage Ā(s) = E[A|s] adds a fixed term Ā(s)(q − p) to the update:
- **Positive-advantage prefixes:** the trainer is pulled toward the corrupted sampler. Since the sampler is rebuilt from the trainer every step, the corruption is applied again on top each time and the error builds up.
- **Negative-advantage prefixes:** the update pushes KL(q‖p) up without limit. That widens the mismatch, which makes the term bigger: a feedback loop.
- **IS weights and clipping:** any truncated weight w leaves a leftover term Ā(m − |m|p), with m = q·w. This is why they slow the drift but do not stop it, and why tighter clipping can make it worse.

**The fix.** Per token the loss is now

`−A [ w(y) log p(y) − Σ_v sg(q_v·w_v) log p_v ]`

where w = 1 when no correction is passed. In logits the gradient is −A(e_y − q) instead of −A(e_y − p). The new score has zero mean under q for every prefix, so any advantage offset cancels again and the drift term is gone. When q = p, Σ_v p_v∇log p_v = 0 exactly, so the loss is identical to REINFORCE on-policy. It stays active with `correction=None`, and with a correction it uses q·w(p/q) via the existing `log_mass`.

**How q is known.** The term is computed in a new function, `sampler_baseline`:
- **Full sampler logprobs:** exact.
- **Top-k head:** q is known on the head and at the sampled token. The leftover sampler mass is spread over the other tokens in proportion to p. The gradient identity Σ_v p_v∇log p_v = 0 avoids any full-vocabulary scatter.
- **Sampled token only:** this reduces to a per-token weight (1 − q(y))/(1 − p(y)), which only partly removes the bias. Hence the top-k config.

**Checks.** A numerical test confirmed the logit gradients match the formula in all three modes, and with the IS corrections I tried. Mini-task runs (600 steps, noise 0.3, eval reward):

| Setup | Plain REINFORCE | New loss |
|---|---|---|
| Default vocab | plateau about 0.70 | about 0.83 with top-k 4 or full q |
| +100 tail tokens | collapsed to 0 | about 0.80–0.84 with top-k 2 or 8 (two seeds at top-k 8) |

In the tail-token setup the token-only fallback rose to only 0.09, naive token IS got 0.54 and TIS 0.60. Adding TIS on top of the new loss gave 0.63, worse than without it, so the submission uses no correction. None of this ran on GPU or on Qwen3-0.6B. k = 64 is a choice I did not tune on the real model.

Files are in `/workspace`:
- `losses.py`
- `REPORT.md`
